answer: Each epoch the ledger cuts decoys from real submissions, swapping three words and inverting a clause, then leaves them where a scraper will find them, a false zenith parked on the public queue. Any answer sharing an eight-word run with a decoy is voided, and the wallet funding it loses emission for six epochs. A farm must then write every account's text from scratch, near 4,000 fresh answers daily for a thousand identities, about $60,000 of reader time before anything clears. Copied work leaks the signal of its origin the way a pearl keeps the grit that seeded it.
